lit.\u0027¿Cuál NO reacciona con NaNH₂ como: "Which one does NOT react with NaNH₂ as an acid?"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eCon \u003cb\u003eH₂/P:
"

With H₂/Pd-C the alkyne goes all the way to the alkane. The Lindlar catalyst (poisoned Pd) stops at the cis alkene, by syn addition of both H atoms. Reduction with Na in liquid NH₃ gives the trans alkene through a radical anion. Observe the product's geometry.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eEl \u003cb\u003eHBr\u:
"

HBr adds across the triple bond: H goes to the carbon with more H and Br to the more substituted one, via a vinyl cation. With one equivalent the bromoalkene is obtained; with excess, the geminal dibromide. Compare the product of a terminal and an internal alkyne.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eEl H de un \u003cb\u0:
"

The H of a terminal alkyne is acidic (pKa ≈ 25), much more than that of an alkene (44) or an alkane (50), because the carbanion's lone pair sits in an sp (50% s) orbital, closer to the nucleus. A strong base such as NaNH₂ removes it to form an acetylide, a nucleophile useful for lengthening chains. 2-Butyne has no terminal H and does not react.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eEn un \u003cb\u003eal:
"

In an alkyne the two triple-bond carbons are sp hybridized. The C≡C bond (1.20 Å) is shorter than C=C (1.34 Å) and the four atoms H–C≡C–C lie on a straight line (180°). One σ and two π bonds (perpendicular to each other) form the triple bond. Switch between propyne, 1-butyne and 2-butyne.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eLa \u003cb\u003ehidra:
"

Hg²⁺-catalyzed hydration follows Markovnikov's rule and gives an unstable enol that tautomerizes to a ketone. Hydroboration–oxidation is anti-Markovnikov: a terminal alkyne yields an aldehyde. A symmetrical internal alkyne gives a single ketone.

"

lit.\u0027«Alquino» y «Reacción»: hidrogenac: '“Alkyne” and “Reaction”: hydrogenation (Lindlar or Na/NH₃), hydration or HBr addition.'

lit.\u0027Adición sin al mismo lado: alqueno: "Syn addition on the same side: cis (Z) alkene."
lit.\u0027Anión radical más estable trans.\u: "The radical anion is more stable trans."
lit.\u0027Anti-Markovnikov: el enol da un al: "Anti-Markovnikov: the enol gives an aldehyde (terminal alkyne)."
lit.\u0027El alquino terminal es ácido porqu: "The terminal alkyne is acidic because the carbanion…"
lit.\u0027El H terminal (pKa ≈ 25) se despro: "The terminal H (pKa ≈ 25) is removed: the acetylide forms, a good nucleophile."
lit.\u0027El H terminal es ácido (pKa ≈ 25): "The terminal H is acidic (pKa ≈ 25) because the sp carbanion has 50 % s character"
